newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mixed, HSFO better supported.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mixed, HSFO better supported.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were narrowly mixed Monday in lackluster trade, with high sulphur helped by stable to firmer bunkers and slightly stronger crude, industry sources said.

"High sulphur may have a little upside - bunkers are up a little, but it's still hard to move midgrades (lower sulphurs)," said one cash trader, noting little demand despite prospects for cooler East Coast weather later this week.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged to down slightly in the $15.25-50 a barrel area, with May paper up slightly from Friday to the low-$15s on firmer crude.
NYH 2.2 percent notionally was flat to modestly higher at $14.00-25, helped by firmer bunkers, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent gained a quarter to $15.00-25, while three percent notionally held steady at $13.25-50.
Traders said there was no word on a Midwest utility tender for 130,000 barrels of 0.7 percent material.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas gained more than 10 cents Monday to the mid-$2.20s/mmBtu, or $14.18 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed more than five cents to the high-$1.90s/mmBtu, or $12.47 a barrel.
